Jesus rebuked him: "Be quiet!" he said sharply. "Come out of him!" The demon threw the man down before them all and came out without injuring him.

The crowd's reaction: "All the people were amazed and said to each other, 'What is this teaching? With authority and power he gives orders to impure spirits and they come out!'" (Luke 4:36)

When evening came, the people brought to Jesus all who had various kinds of sickness, and laying his hands on each one, he healed them. Moreover, demons came out of many people, shouting, "You are the Son of God!" But he rebuked them and would not allow them to speak.

## What It Reveals

Jesus never negotiated with demons; he silenced them.

He does not argue, he does not have long conversations, he gives them no platform. He commands, and they obey. Why? Because he came precisely for this: "The one who does what is sinful is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the devil's work." (1 John 3:8)

## A Necessary Balance

There are two errors to avoid, as writer C. S. Lewis showed well in the preface to his book "The Screwtape Letters": one is not believing in the existence of demons; the other is believing in them and showing excessive and unhealthy interest in them.

The Bible does not see a demon behind every problem. It distinguishes sickness and possession. Jesus healed some sick people simply, and delivered others. Depression can have medical, psychological, relational causes. But the Bible also does not deny the reality of a hostile spiritual world that can oppress, torment, bind.

## For Your Life

Do not live in fear. The one in you is greater than the one in the world (1 John 4:4). Demons trembled before Jesus; they still tremble before his name.

And do not live in naivety either. If you observe in your life or that of someone close to you unexplainable torments, paralyzing fears without cause, occult practices in the family, thoughts of death that return with force, do not stay alone. Talk to mature church leaders. In prayer, with calmness and authority, the name of Jesus sets free.

pratique.texte: If the subject of demons frightens you, learn 1 John 4:4 by heart today and say it aloud. You are on the side of the Victor.
Don't see a demon everywhere. For a physical or psychological health problem, also see a doctor. Prayer and care go together, and discernment is made with mature leaders.

If you experience repeated torments (nightmares, unexplainable fears, thoughts of death), pray with calmness: "In Jesus's name, I command you to be quiet and depart." Then talk about it this week with a leader in your church.

days.question: Do I tend to ignore the reality of spiritual warfare, or do I see it everywhere? How can I find Jesus's balance?
days.priere: Lord Jesus, you came to destroy the works of the devil, and you defeated them at the cross. I do not want to live in fear or in naivety. Give me your discernment and your authority, to be free and to help others be set free. Amen.
days.aRetenir: Jesus never negotiated with demons; he silenced them.

days.title: In the Name of Jesus Christ
days.meditation:
## The Story

In Philippi, Paul and his companions encounter a young slave girl possessed by a spirit of divination. She predicts the future, and her masters make much money through her. She follows Paul for several days, crying out: "These men are servants of the Most High God, and they proclaim to you the way of salvation."

What she says is true. But the source is evil. And finally: "She did this for many days. But Paul, greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, 'I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.' And it came out that very hour." (Acts 16:18)

## What It Reveals

Paul doesn't perform long rituals. He doesn't shout for hours. He speaks to the spirit—one sentence, in the name of Jesus Christ. And the spirit comes out that very hour.

It's not the volume of your voice that casts out demons; it's the name you speak.

Paul explains elsewhere why this name has such authority: "Therefore God also has highly exalted Him and given Him the name which is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth," (Philippians 2:9-10)

Also notice that Paul doesn't accept the spirit's "advertising," even when it seems favorable. Not everything that speaks of God is necessarily from God. Discernment is essential.

## The Price of Freedom

This young girl's deliverance comes at a cost. Her masters, seeing their source of income disappear, drag Paul and Silas before the magistrates. They are beaten with rods and thrown into prison, with their feet in stocks.

And at midnight, instead of complaining, they pray and sing praises to God. The other prisoners hear them. An earthquake shakes the prison—the doors fly open, and everyone's chains fall off. The jailer, terrified, asks: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" And that night, he and his whole household believe and are baptized.

One deliverance led to another, and praise opened prisons.

## For Your Life

Freeing someone sometimes disturbs interests: those who profit from the occult, from addictions, from exploitation. Don't be surprised if you face opposition.

But remember this above all: your authority doesn't depend on your strength, your experience, or your eloquence. It rests on the name of Jesus, which is above every name. When you pray for someone who is bound, speak with calm and confidence, in the name of Jesus.

And in your nights of prison, when everything seems locked, do as Paul and Silas did: praise God. Praise isn't only a response to victory; it's often a weapon that precedes it.

pratique.texte: When you pray against oppression (fear, torment, confusion), do it in one clear, calm sentence: "In the name of Jesus Christ, I command you to leave." No need to shout or repeat for hours.
Not everything that speaks of God is from God. If you follow "prophets," seers, or spiritual influencers, verify their message in the light of Scripture and ask advice from mature leaders.
If you're going through a "prison" right now, choose a moment this week to praise God aloud, even if you don't feel like it: a song, a psalm, a list of thanksgivings.

days.question: Am I relying on the name of Jesus, or on my own spiritual strength, when facing spiritual warfare?
days.priere: Lord Jesus, Your name is above every name. Before it, every knee bends. Teach me to speak it with faith and calm to free those who are bound. Give me discernment, and in my nights, teach me to praise You until the doors open. Amen.
days.aRetenir: It's not the volume of your voice that casts out demons; it's the name you speak.

days.title: Closing the Doors
days.meditation:
## The Story

In Ephesus, a city famous for its magic and sorcerers, God works extraordinary miracles through Paul's hands: the sick are healed, evil spirits come out.

Then some Jewish exorcists, the seven sons of a man named Sceva, try to imitate Paul. They say to the demons: "I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul proclaims!" And here is the reply of the evil spirit: "The evil spirit answered and said, 'Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?'" (Acts 19:15)

The man possessed jumps on them, overpowers them, and puts them to flight, naked and wounded.

## What It Reveals

The name of Jesus is not a magic formula. The sons of Sceva knew the name, but they didn't know the person. They spoke of "Jesus whom Paul proclaims," not "Jesus my Lord."

You don't cast out demons with a formula; you cast them out with a relationship.

Spiritual authority comes from belonging. It's because you are God's child, submitted to Jesus, filled with His Spirit, that you can use His name.

## The Great Housecleaning of Ephesus

And the story doesn't end there: "Many of those who had believed came confessing and telling their deeds. And many of those who had practiced magic brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. And they counted up the value of them, and it totaled fifty thousand pieces of silver. So the word of the Lord grew mightily and prevailed." (Acts 19:18-20)

Believers, not pagans, come to confess their practices. They had believed in Jesus, but they had kept their magic books at home. And they burn them publicly. Fifty thousand pieces of silver: an enormous sum, years of wages. They don't try to resell them. They destroy them.

The result: the word of the Lord grows mighty and prevails.

## For Your Life

Many Christians today have believed in Jesus but still keep "magic books": horoscopes consulted "for fun," tarot cards, past visits to a fortune teller or witch doctor, amulets and lucky charms, spiritist practices, objects tied to rituals, certain practices presented as "wellness" but linked to spirits. The Bible is clear on this (Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

These things are open doors. You can pray for a long time to be free, but if you leave the doors open, freedom won't last.

Today, do as the believers in Ephesus did: confess, renounce, and get rid of what's connected to it. This isn't superstition in reverse: it's an act of loyalty to Jesus alone.

pratique.texte: Ask the Holy Spirit to remind you of any occult practice in your life or your family (fortune-telling, horoscopes, tarot, witch doctor, spiritism, amulets). Write them down honestly.
For each one, pray aloud: "In the name of Jesus, I renounce… and I close this door." Then get rid of the related objects—don't sell or give them away.
If these practices were significant (rituals, pacts, repeated consultations), ask church leaders to pray with you. You shouldn't do this housecleaning alone.

days.question: Do I still have, in my life or my home, "magic books" that I've never burned? Do I know Jesus personally, or only "the Jesus that others proclaim"?
days.priere: Lord Jesus, I don't want to know You by name only, but personally. I renounce any occult practice from my past and my family, and I close all the doors I've opened. I belong to You alone. May Your word grow mighty in my life. Amen.
days.aRetenir: You don't cast out demons with a formula; you cast them out with a relationship.

days.title: What Bends You
days.meditation:
## The Story

One Sabbath day, Jesus is teaching in a synagogue. There is a woman bent over for eighteen years. Eighteen years looking at the ground. Eighteen years without seeing people's faces, without seeing the sky. "And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bent over and could in no way raise herself up. But when Jesus saw her, He called her to Him and said to her, 'Woman, you are loosed from your infirmity.' And He laid His hands on her, and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God." (Luke 13:11-13)

The synagogue leader objects: healing is not done on the Sabbath! And Jesus answers him: "So ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound—think of it—for eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath?" (Luke 13:16)

## What It Reveals

First, notice that Jesus sees her. She's not crying out, she's not asking anything. She's there, invisible, as she probably has been for years in this synagogue. Jesus sees her, calls her, speaks to her, and lays His hands on her.

Second, Jesus names the cause: "Satan bound this woman." It wasn't just a back problem; there was a spiritual chain. And Jesus frees her by laying His hands on her: healing and deliverance are intertwined.

Finally, He calls her "a daughter of Abraham." He restores her dignity and her place among God's people, before all those who may have looked down on her.

Jesus doesn't ask you to straighten up by yourself: He lays His hand on what bends you.

## The Invisible Chains

Not all chains are visible. Some people walk straight, but their soul has been bent for years: shame that makes them lower their eyes, childhood trauma, abuse never spoken of, bitterness that gnaws, a hidden addiction, a curse word that returns ("you're worthless," "you'll end up like your father").

Freeing means more than casting out demons spectacularly. It means helping people be freed from what holds them bent: through prayer, forgiveness, the truth of God's Word, companionship, and sometimes professional help.

## For Your Life

What bends you? How long has it been? Eighteen years, maybe longer. You may have become so used to it that you believe it's your normal posture. Jesus doesn't see you as a hopeless case. He sees you as a son or daughter of Abraham, who has the right to freedom.

And around you, who is bent, invisible, in the back of the room? Jesus noticed this woman. Ask Him for eyes to see those no one sees.

pratique.texte: Write what has weighed on you for a long time: shame, fear, trauma, bitterness, addiction, negative words. Present it to Jesus and ask Him to lay His hand on that specific place.
If a curse has been spoken over you ("you're worthless," "you'll never succeed"), pray: "In the name of Jesus, I reject this word and I receive what God says about me." Then read Ephesians 2:10.
For trauma or abuse, seek companionship: a trained pastor, a support group, and if necessary a healthcare professional. God also frees through skilled people.

days.question: What has held me "bent" for so long that I've become used to it? Who around me is bent and invisible?
days.priere: Lord Jesus, You see what bends me for so many years. Lay Your hand on me. I receive Your word: I am freed. Straighten me so I glorify You. And open my eyes to those bent around me, that I might bring them Your freedom. Amen.
days.aRetenir: Jesus doesn't ask you to straighten up by yourself: He lays His hand on what bends you.

days.title: Staying Free
days.meditation:
## What the Word Says

Jesus speaks to Jews who have just believed in him. And he tells them the secret of a freedom that lasts: "Jesus said to the Jews who had believed in him, 'If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples; and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.'" (John 8:31-32)

Then he adds: "So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." (John 8:36)

## Free Without Knowing It

On January 1, 1863, in the middle of the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln signs the Emancipation Proclamation: enslaved people in the rebellious Confederate States are declared free. But in Texas, far from the fighting, the news doesn't circulate, or it's hidden. It isn't until June 19, 1865, more than two years later, that soldiers arrive in Galveston and publicly announce freedom to the enslaved people. For two and a half years, hundreds of thousands of people were free on paper, and lived still in chains, because no one had announced the news to them.

You can be free on paper and still live in chains, if no one has announced it to you.

That's why the three mandates go together. Freedom was purchased at the cross, but it must be announced, and it must be applied in lives.

## Staying Free

Paul writes to the Galatians, who were falling back into old slavery: "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery." (Galatians 5:1)

Being set free is a moment. Staying free is a journey. Jesus told a troubling story: an unclean spirit comes out of a person, then returns and finds the house "empty, swept, and put in order." It returns with seven other spirits worse than itself (Matthew 12:43-45). An empty house is a vulnerable house.

The secret, according to Jesus, is to "abide in his word." Fill the house. After a deliverance, it's not enough to drive out what was evil; you must let Jesus, his Word, and his Spirit occupy the whole place.

## For Your Life

If you have been set free from something (an addiction, an oppression, a fear, a habit), protect your freedom. Fill your life with the Word, with praise, with fellowship, with service. Close the doors you had opened. Surround yourself with people who help you stand firm.

And remember the enslaved people of Texas. Around you, people are free on paper, because Jesus paid for them, but they don't know it yet. Someone must announce the news to them. Why not you?

pratique.texte: If you have been set free from something, choose three habits to fill your life this week: a daily time in the Word, a time of praise, a moment with brothers and sisters.
Choose a verse about freedom (John 8:36, Galatians 5:1, Romans 8:2) and memorize it. Say it out loud each time the old chains try to come back.

Think of someone who still lives "in chains" without knowing that Jesus can set them free. Pray for them, then find an opportunity to tell them, in your own words, that there is true freedom in Jesus.

days.question: What have I been set free from, and how am I protecting that freedom? Is my "house" filled, or empty and swept?
days.priere: Lord Jesus, if you set me free, I am truly free. I want to abide in your word, and let you fill my whole house. Keep me from returning under the yoke. And send me to announce freedom to those who don't yet know it's for them. Amen.
days.aRetenir: Being set free is a moment. Staying free is a journey.

days.title: You Have Received Freely
days.meditation:
## Part 5: Sent Out

Here we are on the last day. We started with Jesus sending out the twelve in Luke 9. We finish with the same commission, told by Matthew, in more detail.

## What the Word Says

"Go and say: 'The kingdom of heaven is near.' Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those who have leprosy, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give." (Matthew 10:7-8)

Announce: "The kingdom of heaven is near." Heal: "Heal the sick, cleanse those who have leprosy." Set free: "Drive out demons." And even "raise the dead": nothing is too great for the kingdom.

Then this phrase that sums it all up: "Freely you have received; freely give."

## Freely

Everything you have received from God, you received freely: forgiveness, peace, healing, freedom, the Spirit, the gifts. You paid nothing, deserved nothing. And Jesus asks you to give it the same way.

That means two things. First, no commerce: you don't charge for a prayer, a deliverance, a healing. Second, no pride: what you give is not yours. You're just a distributor of what you've received.

## Sheep Among Wolves

Jesus doesn't hide the reality: "I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves." (Matthew 10:16)

Shrewdly as snakes: with wisdom, discernment, intelligence. Don't be naive, know the terrain, respect people, choose your words. Innocent as doves: with purity, without ulterior motives, without manipulation, without seeking your own interest.

The mission isn't always easy. There will be refusals, mockery, sometimes opposition. But Jesus sends, and he goes with you.

## For Your Life

Announce, heal, set free: this isn't the job of a few, it's the DNA of all.

For 21 days, you've seen Jesus do it, then the apostles, then the Church. Now it's your turn. Not necessarily on a stage or in a distant country. Where you live: in your family, in your neighborhood, at your work, in your school, in your church, on your networks.

Announcing is telling what Jesus did for you, and inviting. Healing is daring to say "Can I pray for you?" to someone who is sick, and walking alongside them. Setting free is helping someone close the doors and abide in the truth.

You have received freely. Now go, and give freely.

pratique.titre: Your Plan for the Next 30 Days
pratique.texte: Write one concrete step for each mandate: a person to announce Jesus to, a sick person to pray for, a person to walk with toward freedom. Put a date next to each name.
Before each action, ask yourself: Am I acting with wisdom (respect, discernment, right timing) and with purity (without manipulation, without seeking my glory)?

pratique.titre: Don't Keep This Plan to Yourself
pratique.texte: Invite one or two people to do this plan with you, or to live these three mandates together: pray once a week, go out in pairs to visit the sick, share your testimonies.

days.question: Concretely, how will I live these three mandates (announce, heal, set free) in the next 30 days?
days.priere: Lord Jesus, I have received freely your forgiveness, peace, healing, freedom, and your Spirit. I want to give freely. Send me to announce your kingdom, heal the sick, and set the captives free, where you have placed me. Make me shrewd as a snake and innocent as a dove. Here I am, send me. Amen.
